reason: Hairs radiating from a common point in tufts are stellate hairs. Annotate the quality on the hair (trichome), with the vein axil as its position, rather than on the leaf.
An 'underground stem stocklike' is a rootstock, which PO has as a RELATED synonym of rhizome. The word names the part, not a quality.
Sub-leathery is the English form of subcoriaceous (leathery is an EXACT synonym of PATO_0104032 coriaceous).

Valleculate means having valleculae, i.e. longitudinal grooves. This is the same reading as 'canaliculate' in the previous review (PATO_0002255 grooved).

label: vasiform
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a vase: tubular, somewhat narrowed in the middle or below the mouth and flaring towards the mouth. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991104 urceolate, which is contracted at the mouth, and PATO:0002521 funnel-shaped.
reason: A standard corolla-shape term with a clear meaning that is distinct from urceolate (urn-shaped) and funnel-shaped. Low frequency so far.
'Column without a (column) foot' in orchids states that the column foot is absent. The part already exists as a FLOPO class.
States the absence of a part that has no class ('hooked apical projection'), so the absence pattern has no bearer to apply to. Review it again if such an appendage class is added.

Fusion of the fruit with an organ of a different kind, stated with its second term. This is adnate plus 'towards' the perianth.

Says that some pinna pairs are reduced so that they look like aerophores (FLOPO_0986109). This is a resemblance of a stage or position in a series, not a stable quality, and it is too rare for a '-like' value.
'Leaves/leaflets alternately arranged' = alternate. It follows pattern 16 (quality of a whole towards its parts).
Secondary veins joined in arches near the margin is brochidodromous venation. The quality inheres in the leaf (lamina), not in the single vein.

label: balusterform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a baluster: elongate, swollen in its lower part and narrowed above, with a wider top. NOTE: Used of filament collars and antheropodia; sibling of FLOPO:0991306 napiform and FLOPO:0991168 moniliform.
reason: A specific term for the swollen-and-constricted shape of stamen appendages, with no PATO or FLOPO match. It is rare, so treat it as a candidate and keep it only if more floras use it.
A petiole or midvein widened at its base. This follows the 'expanded' → dilated rule, with base as the region of the bearer (part of a part).
A margin with two orders of crenate-serrate teeth is doubly toothed. Doubly serrate (FLOPO:0991221) would ignore the crenate part.
Cymbiform → scaphoid was decided in the previous review. 'Broadly' is a modifier only.
'Anthers broken up into many locelli' means locules divided into locelli, which is the definition of locellate. The number (20-60) goes to the count pattern.
Maculate = spotted (as in the FNA candidates). The brown is the colour of the spots, which is a separate part-and-quality annotation if wanted.
A choripetalous (polypetalous, dialypetalous) corolla has free petals. Following pattern 16, this is 'corolla free towards its petals', like 'petals separate'.
